review_notes: I read the whole file: the ChartBoundaryInvariant class, its C^1 instance, the EvalSurface bundle, and evalSurface with eval_surface_hypotheses. The class states a property of Mathlib's manifold boundary: charts send boundary points to the frontier of the extended target. A grep of Mathlib/Geometry for that statement and class name found no existing counterpart. Mathlib proves this only for smooth manifolds, through `isBoundaryPoint_iff_of_mem_atlas`, which the instance uses directly. The class is therefore a different, weaker-assumption interface, not a competing definition. EvalSurface is a data bundle of existing typeclasses, and its docstring explains why it exists (blueprint references and passing the hypotheses as data). I found no Mathlib structure that bundles these instances. I did not search every Mathlib directory exhaustively for similar bundles. I found no clear case for consolidation.
